Northwind Robotics raises $45M Series B to scale warehouse automation deployments

Northwind Robotics closed a $45 million Series B led by Candler Ventures to expand deployment capacity for its autonomous picking systems.

All releasesPublish your own

SEATTLE, WA, UNITED STATES — October 22, 2026

Northwind Robotics, Inc., a warehouse automation company, today announced it has raised $45 million in Series B funding led by Candler Ventures, with participation from Hollowbrook Capital and existing investors. The round brings total funding to $78 million.

The company said the capital will fund deployment capacity for its NW-300 autonomous picking system, which it claims reduces manual pick time by 41% in customer facilities. Northwind currently operates in 62 warehouses across North America and Europe and expects to reach 150 sites by the end of 2027.

Northwind also announced it is opening a second manufacturing facility in Guadalajara, Mexico, in the first quarter of 2027, creating approximately 180 roles.

“The constraint on warehouse automation has never been demand. It has been the number of teams we can physically deploy. This round is about deployment capacity, not marketing.”

— Priya Raghunathan, Chief Executive Officer, Northwind Robotics

About Northwind Robotics, Inc.

Northwind Robotics builds autonomous picking systems for mid-size and enterprise warehouses. Founded in 2019, the company operates 62 deployed sites across North America and Europe.
